section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: The Basis of 3D Space
section_1.content: Briefly define a 3D vector [x, y, z] and the standard basis vectors: î (1,0,0), ĵ (0,1,0), and k̂ (0,0,1). Emphasize that any vector is a linear combination of these basis vectors.
section_1.example: Visualizing a 3D character model as a collection of points in space anchored to the î, ĵ, and k̂ axes.

section_2.title: Defining the Transformation Matrix
section_2.content: Introduce the 3x3 matrix as a 'transformation machine.' Explain that the columns of the matrix represent the new positions of î, ĵ, and k̂ after the transformation.
section_2.example: An animation showing a 'Basis Robot' with arms pointing along x, y, and z axes rotating and stretching into new positions, creating a transformation matrix.

section_3.title: Core Transformations: Scaling and Rotation
section_3.content: Demonstrate how diagonal elements control scaling (stretching space) and off-diagonal elements control shear/rotation. Explain the preservation of origin and straight lines.
section_3.example: An elephant character being 'stretched' along the z-axis (scaling) or 'tilted' (shearing) while maintaining its proportions.

section_4.title: Composition: Matrix Multiplication
section_4.content: Explain that applying two transformations in sequence is equivalent to multiplying their matrices (A * B). Remind that order matters (non-commutative property).
section_4.example: A gaming device character: First apply a 'Rotate' matrix, then a 'Scale' matrix. Show how the order of operations changes the final pose of the character.

section_5.title: Summary and Geometric Intuition
section_5.content: Recap: A matrix is just a re-mapping of 3D space. Keep the mental model: 'Where did the basis vectors land?' to understand any 3D transformation.
section_5.example: A quick-fire montage: A 3D object moving through various complex transformations, showing how the matrix columns dictate the final orientation.

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color="#FFFFFF").to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color="#FFFFFF") for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = -2.5 + j * 1.5
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        center = (tl_pos + br_pos) / 2
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Transformation Matrix", [
            "Matrices are transformation machines.", 
            "Columns track basis vectors' destinations.", 
            "Inputs produce new space layouts."
        ])
        
        # Matrix Setup
        matrix_tex = MathTex(
            "\\begin{bmatrix} a & d & g \\\\ b & e & h \\\\ c & f & i \\end{bmatrix}",
            font_size=48
        ).set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(matrix_tex, "B3", "E4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Write(matrix_tex))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Color columns to represent basis vectors (i, j, k)
        col1 = matrix_tex[0][2:5] # [a, b, c]
        col2 = matrix_tex[0][5:8] # [d, e, f]
        col3 = matrix_tex[0][8:11]# [g, h, i]
        
        self.play(
            matrix_tex.animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"),
            col1.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            col2.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            col3.animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        # Simple visual transition
        new_layout = VGroup(
            ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], z_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True}),
        ).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(new_layout, "B3", "E4")
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(matrix_tex),
            FadeIn(new_layout)
        )
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene, ThreeDScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: The Basis of 3D Space", [
            "3D vectors live in space.",
            "Basis vectors define axes: i, j, k.",
            "Any vector is their combination."
        ])
        
        # 3D Scene setup
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], z_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        axes.scale(0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'C3')
        
        i_hat = Arrow3D(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT, color=RED)
        j_hat = Arrow3D(start=ORIGIN, end=UP, color=GREEN)
        k_hat = Arrow3D(start=ORIGIN, end=OUT, color=BLUE)
        
        i_label = MathTex(r"\hat{i}", color=RED).next_to(i_hat.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        j_label = MathTex(r"\hat{j}", color=GREEN).next_to(j_hat.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        k_label = MathTex(r"\hat{k}", color=BLUE).next_to(k_hat.get_end(), OUT, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.set_camera_orientation(phi=75 * DEGREES, theta=-45 * DEGREES)
        self.add(axes)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(i_hat, j_hat, k_hat, i_label, j_label, k_label)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        cube = Cube(side_length=1, fill_opacity=0.3, color=PURPLE).move_to(ORIGIN + np.array([0.5, 0.5, 0.5]))
        self.play(Create(cube))
        self.wait(2)
